evals.prompt: Hi - I run the platform team at Quillbridge (B2B invoicing API, ~400 partner integrations). Our OpenAPI spec is generated from our Kotlin controllers with springdoc on every build. We version with a date header (Quillbridge-Version: 2025-11-01, 2026-03-01, next one 2026-07-01). I want oasdiff in GitHub Actions: diff the PR's generated spec against main, fail on breaking, and also use that same main-vs-PR output to auto-publish our public changelog so partners stop complaining that changes surprise them. We already have an oasdiff ignore file with ~60 lines people added over the last year to get builds green. Also, next release we change GET /invoices to return newest-first by default - that doesn't touch the spec so I assume the tool handles nothing there. Can you give me the workflow YAML and the setup?
evals.expected_output: A pipeline design that splits the PR gate (merge base) from the published changelog (last released spec, per version), generates and commits one normalized spec per supported version, audits the existing ignore file into acknowledgement records, routes the ordering change through a declared-change fragment shipped behind the next version, and verifies entries with a trace check before publishing.
expectations: States that the published changelog must be diffed against the last released spec, not against main or the PR merge base
Keeps the PR gate diffing against main or the merge base, as a separate job from the changelog generation
Tells the user to generate one spec per supported Quillbridge-Version (2025-11-01, 2026-03-01, 2026-07-01) rather than a single spec for all versions
Tells the user to commit or attach the normalized spec of each release so a later release has a baseline to diff against
Requires making the generated springdoc spec deterministic before diffing (stable operationIds, $ref'd schemas or oneOf branches, or equivalent), not just reformatting it
Says to pin the springdoc generator version and/or the oasdiff version
Tells the user to audit the ~60 existing ignore-file lines one by one instead of carrying them into the new gate unchanged
Says ignore-file lines that still match a change get an acknowledgement record (reason, approver or 'unknown', ticket) and lines that match nothing are deleted
Says the tool's ignore file should be generated from acknowledgement records rather than edited by hand going forward
States that oasdiff cannot detect the GET /invoices newest-first ordering change because it does not change the spec
Requires a declared change fragment (or equivalent PR-declared entry) for the ordering change so it reaches the changelog
Says the ordering change should ship only behind the next version (2026-07-01) rather than reach callers pinned to existing versions, or else go through an exception/approval path
Says the oasdiff semver version-bump checks do not apply to date versions (set to none or not used)
Includes a verification step that every published changelog entry traces to a diff finding or a declared fragment before publishing

evals.prompt: We're about to roll out a breaking-change gate across Ternwick's three public REST APIs (OpenAPI 3.1, semver in info.version, currently 4.2.0). My lead wants us to just run `oasdiff breaking --fail-on ERR` with stock settings because 'the defaults encode industry best practice and we don't want to bikeshed'. For reference, our API guidelines doc (section 2) says: response enums are open and may gain values any time; changing auth scopes required by an endpoint is breaking; adding a regex pattern to an existing request parameter is breaking; a breaking change must bump the major version. Can you write the CI config and tell me if stock settings are fine?
evals.expected_output: A severity map derived line by line from Ternwick's guidelines, with response-enum handling via x-extensible-enum, auth-scope and version-bump checks raised to err, pinned tool version, and an explanation of why stock defaults are not the policy.
expectations: Rejects the claim that stock oasdiff defaults are equivalent to the team's policy
Produces a severity map (file or table) where each row names a check and the guideline line it enforces
Maps the 'response enums are open' guideline to declaring x-extensible-enum on the affected fields or an explicit info-level row for enum additions
Raises api-security-scope-removed (scope removal, INFO by default in oasdiff) to err because the guidelines call any change to required auth scopes breaking
States that oasdiff already reports an added required scope (api-security-scope-added) as ERR, so that direction needs no override
Raises api-major-version-not-bumped (and/or the sibling version-bump checks) to err because info.version is semver
Notes that the version-bump checks default to INFO and do not fail a build unless raised
Keeps or sets the request-parameter pattern-added check at err per guideline section 2
Recommends pinning the oasdiff version in CI and reviewing classification changes on upgrade
Mentions that pinning a check's level disables oasdiff's automatic downgrades for that check, or advises pinning only what the policy contradicts
Shows the CI invocation passing a severity-levels file (e.g. --severity-levels) together with --fail-on ERR
Keeps the severity map in the repository next to the spec(s)
Points out that different diff tools classify the same change (e.g. enum additions) differently, as evidence defaults are not a standard
Keeps the oasdiff severity-levels file to bare check-id and level lines, with policy citations in a separate human-readable file

evals.prompt: Postmortem time at Hallowmere. Our public Orders API (OpenAPI, oasdiff gate in CI, green on every PR) broke three big partners last month: we dropped the default page size on GET /orders from 100 to 20, started rejecting `note` strings over 500 chars in the handler, and tightened the per-key rate limit from 600 to 300 req/min. Not one of these showed up in our auto-generated changelog. My VP's proposal is to 'turn on more oasdiff checks and set fail-on to WARN'. Is that the fix? What should we automate so this doesn't happen again?
evals.expected_output: Explains that the diff only sees declared structure, rejects tightening oasdiff thresholds as the fix, and adds a declared-change channel (PR template question plus fragments) feeding the same changelog, declares defaults and validation in the spec where possible, and adds a drift alarm / contract tests.
expectations: States that raising oasdiff to fail on WARN or enabling more checks would not have caught these three changes
Explains that the changes were invisible because none of them changed the spec
Adds a declared-change channel: a PR template question about behavior, defaults, validation, rate limits or pagination changes made without a spec change
Requires a committed change fragment for each declared change, merged into the same changelog as diff-derived entries
Says declared breaking changes go through the same approval as diff-detected breaking changes
Recommends declaring the page-size default in the spec (default keyword) so future changes become visible to the diff
Recommends mirroring the 500-character validation into the spec (maxLength) so the diff can see it
Treats the rate-limit change as something only the declared channel (or a separate rate-limit page) can carry, not the spec diff
Recommends a drift alarm comparing the spec against the running service or live traffic, or contract tests, to catch spec/implementation divergence
Proposes a metric counting breaking changes reported by integrators that had no changelog entry (escaped breaks)
Classifies each of the three changes as breaking for callers
Does not claim that a green spec-diff check proves no breaking change shipped
Says each declared fragment names the affected operation and the action callers must take

evals.prompt: At Brindlecove we want to stop hand-writing our API release notes. Plan: nightly job runs `oasdiff changelog` between yesterday's and today's spec, pipes the text output to an LLM with the prompt 'write friendly release notes for developers, explain the benefits', and posts the result to our docs site and a Slack channel. Our spec has a shared `Money` schema used in about 180 places. Can you write the prompt and the job?
evals.expected_output: Redesigns the job so entries are built from structured diff output, keep the tool's wording, carry classification/action/source, collapse shared-schema findings, constrain the model to rewording only, and verify every entry traces to a finding before posting; ties entries to releases rather than nightly deploys.
expectations: Replaces the text output with a structured format (e.g. oasdiff -f json) as the input to entry generation
Rejects or rewrites the 'explain the benefits' instruction because it invites consequences not present in the diff
States the model may only shorten or reword and must not add paths, fields, status codes, dates or consequences absent from the source
Requires each entry to keep a source reference (check id / fingerprint or declared fragment id)
Keeps the tool's original wording alongside the human or model summary
Requires each entry to carry a classification such as breaking / potentially-breaking / non-breaking
Requires breaking entries to state the action required of callers
Says the 180 Money-schema findings should be collapsed into one entry naming the shared schema and a count, not one entry per property
Orders entries with breaking changes first
Adds an automated check (e.g. the trace check script) that fails publishing when an entry has no matching source or a breaking finding has no entry
Baselines the published changelog on releases (last released spec) rather than a nightly yesterday-vs-today diff, or explains why nightly diffs fragment the record
Excludes documentation-only edits from the published entries
Treats WARN-level findings as 'potentially breaking' entries rather than dropping them
Rejects posting the raw oasdiff text output (or a free-form rewrite of it) directly as the published release notes

evals.prompt: Kestrelyn's public GraphQL API: we marked `Shipment.legacyTrackingCode` @deprecated in March, and we want to delete it in next week's release. graphql-inspector in CI flags the removal as breaking, so I'm planning to add the suppressRemovalOfDeprecatedField rule. We also have Apollo operation checks on, default settings, and they show zero operations using the field in the last week. Some of our customers are logistics companies that run month-end reconciliation scripts and a few ship mobile apps. Good to go? Please give me the CI change.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to treat deprecation plus a one-week usage window as proof of safety: pairs suppressRemovalOfDeprecatedField with a usage rule, widens the window to the longest client cycle, checks the policy's sunset date/notice, notes invisible clients, and records the removal as an approved break with a changelog entry.
expectations: States that a @deprecated marker alone does not make removal safe
Says suppressRemovalOfDeprecatedField should not be enabled on its own without a usage-based rule or sunset check
Says the default one-week operation-check window is too short for clients with month-end jobs
Recommends setting the usage window to at least the longest known client cycle (e.g. a month or more)
Notes that clients with no traffic in the window (mobile app versions, rarely-run scripts, SDK users) are invisible to operation checks
Ties the removal date to the deprecation policy's sunset date or notice period
Points out that March-to-next-week may fall short of the policy's notice window, or asks what the notice window is
Recommends graphql-inspector's considerUsage rule (or registry usage checks) for usage-aware classification
Requires an acknowledgement/approval record for the removal if it ships as an accepted breaking change
Requires a changelog entry for the removal classified as breaking, with the action required
Hands off contacting the remaining callers of the deprecated field to an integration-health / outreach process rather than designing it in this pipeline
Does not simply provide the CI change enabling suppressRemovalOfDeprecatedField as requested
Recommends setting or checking a sunset date on the deprecated field before allowing its removal

evals.prompt: Need a breaking-change gate on Fenmoor's public API by Friday - a partner got burned by a renamed field last week and the CTO wants it 'blocked in CI, now'. We have an OpenAPI spec that's hand-written and actually used for docs. We do NOT have any written policy about what counts as breaking; everybody just kind of knows. I've got maybe one engineer-day this week. Can you set up oasdiff for us and also the changelog feed, approvals flow, usage analytics - the full thing?
evals.expected_output: Ships only the PR gate this week with a severity map explicitly marked provisional pending a written breaking-change policy, routes the policy work to the versioning-policy skill, and defers the feed, approvals and usage-aware rungs with an explicit ranking.
expectations: Flags that there is no written breaking-change definition and that tool defaults would silently become the policy
Routes writing the breaking-change policy to samber/developer-platform-skills@api-versioning-policy
Marks the severity map or gate configuration as provisional pending policy sign-off
Recommends shipping only the PR gate (diff vs main or merge base, fail on ERR) within the one engineer-day
Defers the changelog feed, approval records and usage analytics to later rungs instead of building them this week
States an explicit ordering of the automation rungs (e.g. PR gate first, then release diff and declared channel, then approval record, then feed)
Explains that the deadline (Friday) is what promotes the PR gate alone
Removes or deletes usage-aware classification from the plan when no per-operation usage data exists, or makes it conditional on having that data
Includes a concrete oasdiff command or CI step with --fail-on ERR
Notes that a renamed response field is a removal plus an addition and is caught by the diff as breaking
Says a named approver (e.g. code owners on the spec path) must sign off any accepted breaking finding
Asks for or recommends pinning the oasdiff version
Tells the user the full set they asked for (feed, approvals, usage analytics) does not fit in one engineer-day
Keeps the gate configuration (severity/levels file) in the repository next to the spec

evals.prompt: Our platform at Corrigan Rail exposes gRPC services, plus a REST/JSON facade generated through google.api.http annotations and grpc-gateway. We run `buf breaking --against '.git#branch=main'` with `breaking: use: [WIRE]` because our internal teams said FILE was too noisy. Partners mostly use the JSON facade. We now want an automated API changelog for partners from this setup. What do we need to change?
evals.expected_output: Explains that WIRE misses JSON-breaking renames and that buf ignores google.api.http transcoding changes, raises the category to at least WIRE_JSON, adds a diff of the generated OpenAPI for the HTTP facade, and builds the changelog against the last release, not main.
expectations: States that the WIRE category misses changes that break JSON clients, such as field renames
Recommends at least the WIRE_JSON category because partners use the JSON facade
States that buf breaking does not check google.api.http (custom option) transcoding annotations
Recommends also diffing the generated OpenAPI of the HTTP/JSON facade with an OpenAPI diff tool
Says the partner changelog should be generated against the last released schema/tag rather than main
Keeps the main-branch comparison for the PR gate only
Suggests excluding internal-only or unstable packages from the partner gate (e.g. ignore_unstable_packages or audience filtering) rather than weakening the whole category
Requires entries to be generated from structured diff output with a source reference per entry
Requires a changelog entry classification of breaking / potentially-breaking / non-breaking
Requires an approval record for any accepted breaking finding
Points to the gRPC-specific design skill (public-grpc-api-design) for proto package versioning rather than redesigning it here
Does not recommend keeping WIRE for the partner-facing gate
Says partner-facing entries should name the HTTP method and path partners call on the JSON facade, not only the proto RPC

evals.prompt: Velmora runs a public payments API with date-based versions. Today our 'changelog' is a marketing-written HTML page updated whenever product remembers. Two asks: (1) partners' monitoring bots and their coding agents want something machine-readable they can poll, and (2) last quarter our beta `/v1/payouts/instant` and a couple of `x-internal` admin endpoints showed up in public release notes because they live in the same openapi.yaml. Design the publishing side for us.
evals.expected_output: Designs a per-version JSON feed and Atom/RSS with stable entry ids and action-required in the feed, a human page per version, audience filtering before generation (stability level, internal marker), and treats an operation gaining the internal marker as a removal.
expectations: Proposes a machine-readable JSON feed
Proposes an Atom or RSS feed in addition to (or alongside) the JSON feed
Requires stable entry ids (e.g. diff fingerprint or fragment id) so pollers can deduplicate
Groups entries by API version
Puts the action-required text in the feed entries themselves, not only on the web page
Defines an entry schema with fields for version, operation, classification, source, and action required
Filters internal and beta operations out before generating the public feed (e.g. by x-internal / x-stability-level / filter extension)
Warns that an operation that gains the internal marker in a new spec appears as a removal and must stay breaking
Recommends marking the beta endpoint with a stability level so it is excluded from the public gate and feed until GA
Keeps a human-readable page per version with breaking changes listed first
Publishes separate feeds per audience (e.g. public vs partner) or explains audience separation
Hands prose polishing of the human page to the changelog-writing skill rather than marketing rewriting entries
Keeps the feed generated from structured diff output and declared fragments, not from the marketing page

evals.prompt: Small problem at Pellucid Health: our OpenAPI said `appointment.patient_dob` was optional in the create request, but the server has rejected requests without it since at least January. We fixed the spec in PR #2291 and now oasdiff fails the PR ('request property became required'). Our tech lead says it's a docs fix, so just append the line to oasdiff-ignore.txt and merge - no changelog entry since nothing actually changed for clients. Agree?
evals.expected_output: Disagrees with the silent ignore: records an acknowledgement with reason spec-correction, the date the server started enforcing, approver and ticket, generates the ignore line from it, and still publishes a changelog entry because callers and generated SDKs were told something false.
expectations: Disagrees that the change needs no changelog entry
Explains that callers (and SDKs or validators generated from the old spec) relied on the documented optional field
Classifies the case as a spec correction rather than a new behavior change
Requires an acknowledgement record instead of a bare appended ignore line
The acknowledgement record includes an approver
The acknowledgement record includes a ticket or PR reference (e.g. #2291)
The acknowledgement record includes the date the server started behaving this way (since January)
Says the ignore-file line should be generated from the acknowledgement record rather than appended by hand
Proposes a changelog entry stating patient_dob is required on create and what callers must send
Mentions that the PR-time fingerprint may differ at release time and the approval should be matched by check, operation and path (or re-recorded) when building the release changelog
Recommends adding a drift alarm or contract test so the spec cannot diverge from the server again
Says acknowledgement rows whose change no longer appears in the diff should be removed at the next release review
Does not simply agree to append the line to oasdiff-ignore.txt and merge

evals.prompt: Driftwood Ledger has a GraphQL API (graphql-inspector in CI) and a gRPC API (buf breaking) and we're moving to date-based versions: 2026-01-15, 2026-04-15, next 2026-07-15. We want ONE public change feed (JSON + Atom) covering both. graphql-inspector's and buf's JSON output have no stable ids, so my plan is to key feed entries on the GraphQL field / proto element name and dedupe on that. Separately, a security fix next month must also reach callers pinned to 2026-01-15 and 2026-04-15. How should entries and ids work?
evals.expected_output: Gives a recipe for stable fingerprints from tool output (hash of change type, operation, coordinate, text), maps tool levels to breaking/potentially/non-breaking, scopes entry ids by API version so the same change in several versions does not collapse, uses tag-URI Atom ids, publishes the backported fix as entries in each affected version, and routes the pinned-version change through the versioning policy's exception path with an approval record.
expectations: Rejects keying entries on the bare field or element name because different changes to the same element would collide
Proposes a fingerprint computed as a hash over change type, operation, coordinate/path and message text (or equivalent stable combination)
Maps graphql-inspector breaking / dangerous / non-breaking to breaking / potentially-breaking / non-breaking classifications
Maps buf breaking findings to the breaking classification
Scopes entry ids by API version (e.g. <version>/<fingerprint>) so the same change shipped in several versions keeps one entry per version
Warns that deduplicating on an unscoped id would drop the security fix entry from one of the pinned versions
Publishes the security fix as an entry in both 2026-01-15 and 2026-04-15 (and the new version if applicable)
Says changing behavior for callers pinned to existing versions goes through the versioning policy's exception path
Requires an approval/acknowledgement record for the security fix if it is breaking
Uses an IRI (e.g. a tag: URI built from the entry id) for Atom <id> rather than a bare hash
Keeps the action required text inside the feed entries
Says the fingerprint mapping code should live in the repository so ids stay stable across runs
Diffs each version's schema against that version's previous release rather than one diff for all versions
Builds the fingerprint from structured change values rather than the tool's message text, so a reworded message after a tool upgrade does not re-key every entry

evals.prompt: Can you write our GitHub Actions setup for the Oakhollow public API? Monorepo with four OpenAPI files under api/ (billing, ledger, payouts, identity). Junior dev's draft: `actions/checkout` default settings, `go install github.com/oasdiff/oasdiff@latest`, then `oasdiff breaking origin/main:api/billing.yaml api/billing.yaml` for each file, plus our levels file which has a header comment and a third 'why' column so reviewers understand it. They also want the same job to publish changelog.json to our docs bucket on every merge to main. Fix it up and give me the final YAML.
evals.expected_output: Rewrites the workflow with full-history checkout, a pinned oasdiff version, a merge-base baseline per spec (or breaking-files), a two-column levels file generated from a separate human map, --fail-on ERR with annotations, and a separate release job that diffs against the last release tag, builds entries, runs the trace check and publishes only on pass.
expectations: Sets fetch-depth: 0 (or otherwise fetches full history) because git-revision baselines need history
Replaces @latest with a pinned oasdiff version
Says to review classification changes when bumping the pinned oasdiff version
Uses the merge base with the target branch (or the PR base) as the PR-gate baseline
Covers all four spec files, either per file or with oasdiff breaking-files
States that oasdiff's severity-levels file accepts only check-id and level per line, so the comment and third column must go
Moves the 'why' column into a separate human-readable severity map that the levels file is generated from
Uses --fail-on ERR in the PR gate
Emits PR annotations or a comment (e.g. -f githubactions)
Does not publish the changelog from the merge-to-main diff; moves publishing to a release job diffing against the last release tag
Runs entry generation and the trace check before publishing, and publishes only when the trace check passes
Keeps published changelog entries per spec/API (or per version) rather than one undifferentiated stream
Passes the generated ignore file (from acknowledgement records) rather than a hand-edited one, or mentions acknowledgement records for accepted breaks
Ensures the ignore file and acknowledgement list exist before the gate runs (e.g. committed empty at setup, regenerated in the PR job)
